source: the hosted Supabase database, seeded by server/scripts/seedRealisticSubmissions.js — production data, which the owner confirmed is entirely test data and fine to photograph. Server on :4000, Vite on :5173.

capture.theme: forced via localStorage['bc-theme'] in an addInitScript, before the app mounts
capture.settle: document.fonts.ready, all images complete, two animation frames

accounts.anon: no session — what every requester sees
accounts.bc_rep: a requester with report requests of their own; the only way the report-request track appears on the board
accounts.admin: super user and a manager, so the throughput page answers with the team composition
accounts.analyst: bc_report_analyst — one grant, narrowed to report requests on Billing Center

screenshots.state: What a visitor with no session sees at the submit page: filing requires a signed-in person, for every request type. Not a disabled form — the form is not rendered at all, and the endpoint refuses the POST regardless

Submit a service request, signed in — initial state, no request type chosen yet. "Filing as" states who the ticket will belong to, and the name field is gone because the server takes the identity from the session and discards anything the body claims
Defect branch — the questions asked about something that is broken
Defect part-way through, with the readiness rail ticking items off
Enhancement branch — a shorter form, because nothing is broken to describe
Report request, NEW dashboard branch — measures and where they come from. Which application the DATA comes from is asked and never defaulted: it decides which analysts ever see the request

Report request, CHANGE branch — which report, and what should change about it. Only the chosen branch's answers are stored, so the other branch cannot sit on the row contradicting the one that was asked

What a submit attempt with nothing filled in says, and where it says it — per field, not one banner. "You can press Submit with fields empty — we will point them out first" is a promise the form keeps

The duplicate check, with matches. Under each one: whether it happened to you too, how many people have already reported it, and a button whose wording states the condition it is really asking about — "seen this since 18 June?" on a deployed fix, "closed without a fix" on a rejected one

Depth 1 — the ticket is still being worked, so no second ticket is opened. It asks for a line and takes the policy number and date already typed into the form. The blocked tick-box is on every depth, because being stuck today has nothing to do with where somebody else's ticket has got to
Depth 3 — the fix shipped and it is back. It names the release date, says the report will be tagged to the original, and the full form that follows is pre-filled from that ticket rather than blank

The guard, and the reason it exists: a deployed ticket where the date given is BEFORE the fix shipped. Not a regression — the week after any release this is the common case, and treating it as one would bury the real ones. Changing the date turns this sheet back into depth 3 while it is still open
Public status board, signed out — defects and enhancements only. No report request appears at all: they are visible to the person who filed them and nobody else
A row opened to its four-stop track: Reported → Approved → With Service Desk → Deployed, with a date under each stop it actually reached and an em dash under the ones it has not
The grouped filter panel a requester can narrow the board with

The same board as the person who filed the report requests: theirs travel a DIFFERENT track — Reported → Approved → In progress → Delivered — and never mention the Service Desk hand-off a report request does not make
Ticket search opened — "Closest matches", which describes what it found and deliberately never rules on whether a request has already been reported
Admin sign-in. Two kinds of account may sign in: admin (triage) and rep (a requester following their own requests)
The triage queue as a super user, all applications. Only New wears the left stripe — every status having its own colour made the stripe distinguish nothing
The one-click switch between the two kinds of work, set to Report requests — a different column set, and its own saved layout
The grouped admin filter panel
Customize View — which columns and which filters this admin sees, saved per admin and per queue
The bulk action bar, with rows selected — retire, unretire and change visibility in one pass
The queue scoped to one application. An admin sees only the applications they hold a grant on; a super user may switch between all of them

The same queue as bc_report_analyst, whose single grant covers report requests on Billing Center only. No defect is on this screen, and no Manage metadata in the menu. Not the queue with rows hidden — the server sends only what that grant covers, by application AND by request type

`Other`, scoped, with every kind of request showing. It is a working list rather than a holding pen: a system with no configured application to submit to the Service Desk lands here, and so does one nobody has identified yet. Either way the work is still tracked — reports get built from it, and a defect or an enhancement is raised on the Service Desk by hand with its incident number typed back in

A person blocked by an issue somebody else reported, on the queue and without opening anything: the red banner counts them — it counts PEOPLE, so one ticket can contribute several — and the row carries a "1 more blocked" chip in the DEFAULT columns. A toast is not a surface; it is gone the moment nobody was looking
Ticket detail — the Triage tab, which is where it opens: status, reviewer, decision notes and the assignee
The Report tab — what the requester actually wrote, read-only, because a triage decision must not be able to rewrite the report it was made from
The Impact tab on a defect — dollar impact, policies affected and how often it happens
The History tab — every status change with who made it and when, plus where the ticket came from

The Reported again tab — admin only, because the rows carry reporter names, notes and policy numbers while the public surfaces get the count and nothing else. The tab appears only when somebody HAS reported it again; anyone blocked and still waiting is called out at the top with a Mark handled button per person, since the workaround that unblocked one may not cover another's case
The Files tab. Empty on this data set: the seed writes no attachments, because a row pointing at bytes that are not there is worse than an empty tab
The Service Desk tab — the hand-off downstream, and the incident number behind a lock, because for every ticket the portal sent that number is its own record of what it did

A REPORT REQUEST's Report tab — its own layout: what it is for, who to ask or which report, and what they need. It asked a defect's questions until the fifth pass, so an analyst could open one and not read what had been requested
The Delivery pane — the analyst's half of a report request: go-ahead, level of effort, hours by person and day, the assignment trail and the delivery notes
The More actions menu — retire, change visibility, and Redirect, which moves a ticket to another application's queue and records the hand-off

A DEFECT in `Other` — the catch-all working list, for a system with no configured application to submit to the Service Desk and for one nobody has identified yet. Two things in one picture: "Also show it in" under Ownership & tracking, which puts the ticket in an analyst's own queue WITHOUT moving it out of `Other`; and the footer, where Submit is greyed out and the note gives the whole manual procedure — raise it by hand, come back, unlock the number, set Submitted
Add a ticket → New ticket → Defect. An admin filing on somebody else's behalf
Add a ticket → Historical ticket → Defect. The backdated mode: it asks for the dates and the status the ticket already had, and builds the timeline from them
Add a ticket → Historical ticket → Enhancement

Add a ticket → Cleanup, tagged Internal only. A cleanup is stored as a flag on a defect or an enhancement plus its own status — the tag row is what records which, and "Internal only" is the one that was never anybody's bug report
Add a ticket → Report request → Something new. Asks for the measures and where they come from
Add a ticket → Report request → A change to one they already use. Asks which report FIRST, because you cannot describe what should happen to a report before saying which one it is

A reporting analyst adding an application by typing its name in, from under the Application picker. Offered on the REPORT branch only, because what it creates takes report requests and nothing else — and offered only to somebody who works report requests. Creating it also grants it, in the same transaction, to everybody who does: an application is a queue, and one with no grants is visible to nobody but a super user. The same control is in the Redirect dialog, which is where an analyst realises an `Other` request is really Marketing Analytics'
Export to Excel — the field picker, grouped, with presets. The groups come from the SERVER's field list, so a new column cannot be exportable and unlisted
The Report request group of export fields, expanded — including Approved By, Approved Date, Delivery Notes and Hours Logged, which is SUM(hours) computed on read and never a stored column
Import from Excel, step 1 — pick a file and say which kind of ticket the sheet holds. The mode forces the type of every row, which is why a report sheet needs its own

Import step 2 — what each column of the sheet became, with the "Review all N mappings" fold opened. Most columns match themselves; the point of the step is the ones that did not. The first rows are shown as they WILL be imported, before anything is written
Import step 3 — what landed. Rows that came in MINUS a field get their own quieter warnings banner, separate from rows that were skipped, because one list for both would make the difference invisible

Manage metadata — every lookup the portal offers. Editing one renames or withdraws a value on every ticket that holds it, so the three WRITES are super-user only while the READ stays open to every admin
The Statuses panel. Three values are marked "Report requests only" — one table serves every type, and without the marking an admin has no way to know which dropdown a value appears in
What a lookup edit says it will do before it does it — the consequence line, and the lock on a name that is in use

Access management, super-user only. A grant is (person, application, role, request type) — an analyst is an admin grant narrowed to report requests, and a combination the three named scopes cannot express reads as Mixed rather than being rounded to the nearest one
Reporting throughput as a MANAGER — the team composition, with a bar per analyst. The server decides which of the two shapes to answer with; it is not the personal view with rows hidden
The same page with the per-analyst table opened

The same page as somebody who is NOT a manager: four tiles about them, two column charts, and no .tp-bars anywhere — so there is no per-colleague mark on the screen at all. The narrowing is in the QUERY, not in the browser
Submit form, dark theme
Public status board, dark theme
Admin queue, dark theme
Throughput page, dark theme — the two chart colours have their own pair per theme and both were run through the contrast validator
Manage metadata, dark theme
